title: A Sigil for the Spire Revisited
premise: Zephyrine Vane, the Spire's royal food-taster, has spent years dosing himself with poison and memorizing smuggler roads through the Thornfell mountains — the only routes left to the free cities. When a century-old prophecy book surfaces naming tonight's date and a stranger pulled from nowhere into its pages, Zephyrine realizes the prophecy hinges on a sigil hidden in his own family bloodline: proof that the usurper's claim is forged. Hunted by the usurper's inquisitors and shadowed by the prophesied stranger, who may be savior or saboteur, he must carry the sigil through the mountains before the usurper's armies close the passes. In the end, Zephyrine chooses justice outside the law — unsealing the sigil before the free cities' council rather than the crown — igniting not war but a reckoning, and finding in the stranger and the smugglers who sheltered him a family no throne can take.
about_author: Freya Sterling is the pen name of a former line cook who claims she learned everything about court intrigue from restaurant kitchens. She writes fantasy about people whose jobs are smaller than their destinies.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A routine tasting at the Spire turns lethal when a dish carries a poison his immunity barely survives — poison meant for him, not the king. He traces it to a kitchen hand who vanishes through a smuggler's door. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve; Zephyrine realizes someone knows what he really is.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Fleeing through old servant tunnels, he shelters with an archivist friend and finds a century-old prophecy book: tonight's date inked on a page describing 'the taster who swallows truth.' The final line names a stranger arriving out of empty air. Emotional beat: vertigo — his small life was never small.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fell Through Midnight
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, then the stranger's. On the Thornfell road, the prophecy fulfills itself: a man named Corvel steps out of a fold of light with no memory of how he came. He carries half a broken sigil burned into his palm. Emotional beat: wary mutual dependence between two men the world has already scripted.

chapters.title: What the Usurper Forged
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. Piecing together fragments, Corvel recalls glimpses of another life: a royal house erased from records, its sigil split in two. The usurper's armies are already marching on the free cities, erasing evidence as they go. Emotional beat: grief for a self he cannot fully claim, and fear that he was sent as a weapon.

chapters.title: Salt Roads and Smuggler Kings
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The pair hire passage with Maren Quick, a smuggler captain who knew Zephyrine's mother. Maren reveals the Vane family were sigil-keepers, sworn to the erased house. An inquisitor's raid scatters the caravan. Emotional beat: found family forming under fire; first taste of belonging.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Confession
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Cornered in a mountain chapel, Zephyrine learns the kitchen-hand assassin was his own uncle, coerced by the usurper: the Vanes' blood proves the throne stolen, so every Vane must die. He spares his uncle and takes the second half of the sigil from him. Emotional beat: mercy chosen over vengeance — justice begins here.

chapters.title: Where the Pass Closes
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. The army seals the high pass; the only way through is the Undervault, a drowned mine said to be cursed. Maren's crew refuses; three stay anyway. Inside, the sigil halves resonate, showing Corvel visions of the war the usurper wants to reignite. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the terror of knowing what failure costs.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The inquisitor leading the hunt corners them at the vault's mouth — and lowers her blade. She has read the same prophecy and lost family to the usurper's purges. She buys them time with her own arrest. Emotional beat: even the law's hounds can choose; hope hardens into plan.

chapters.title: The Sigil Unsealed
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Climax. They reach the free cities' council as the usurper's herald demands surrender. Before both armies' eyes, Zephyrine and Corvel join the sigil halves; light unmasks the forged lineage and the erased house's true heir — Corvel. The usurper orders fire; her own soldiers, seeing the truth, refuse. Emotional beat: truth as weapon, wielded without a single throne's permission.

chapters.title: A Table Set for Strays
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Resolution. Corvel declines the restored crown, leaving governance to the free cities' council; the inquisitor walks free under amnesty. Zephyrine opens a tavern at the mountain's foot where tasters, smugglers, and strays eat safely together — every dish tested, none poisoned. Emotional beat: quiet joy; inheritance redefined as the family you keep.
